transcript.text: The type changes what to check. Is it a corded vacuum (plugs into the wall), a cordless (battery) one, or a robot?
its corded, plugs in the wall. its the red one Henry with the smiley face

Thanks for confirming that detail. Please try plugging another device into that socket to check if it works, and also inspect the switch on your vacuum. If your plug contains a 13A fuse, you can swap it out while the unit is unplugged. It is also worth looking along the cable for any cuts or damage. Was it the socket, switch or fuse (and is it sorted), is the cable or plug damaged, or is the supply fine?

the lamp works in the socket. theres black tape on the cable near the plug, my son did it ages ago, its bent there. I havent got a screwdriver or spare fuse. it did come on once for a second when I moved the wire then went off

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Exposed or damaged live wiring (or a cracked hob top) can give a serious electric shock. Don't touch it — switch it off at the consumer unit (fuse box) or its isolator switch, keep everyone away, and don't use it again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has made it safe.
